scenarios.title: Build: from an executable to a native port
scenarios.summary: What the tools do to a game's executable, ahead of time, to get a program that runs on a PC.

steps.caption: Stage 1: the loader reads the executable from your own copy of the game and writes out its image, function table, TOC and firmware imports.
Stage 2: the lifter turns every PowerPC function into C++. With --hle-stubs, each firmware import stub becomes a ps3_hle_call(nid).
SPU programs are handled separately: they are pulled out of the executable, and spu_lifter turns each into C. Its 256 KB local store becomes an array.
Stage 3: gen_hle_nids writes the table that maps each NID (the id of a firmware function) to a handler in the runtime.
The lifted code, the NID table and the ps3recomp runtime library are built together with CMake and a C++ compiler.
The result is an ordinary native program for your PC. No emulator runs underneath it.

scenarios.title: Run: what happens when the port plays
scenarios.summary: What the native program does when the game calls the console's firmware, threads, graphics and SPUs.

steps.caption: The lifted game code calls a firmware function. Its stub is now ps3_hle_call(nid).
The NID table finds the handler in the HLE libraries, which are written for this project: input, audio, files, save data and more.
The handler does the real work on your PC: files by ordinary file I/O, a pad through XInput or SDL2, sound through WASAPI or SDL2.
Graphics go through cellGcm to a command processor that stands in for the console's GPU, then to a backend: D3D12 on Windows, Metal on macOS, Vulkan on Linux (opt-in).
The handler returns its result to the dispatcher.
The dispatcher hands it back, and the game code carries on as if the firmware had answered.
Threads, mutexes, memory and file calls go to implementations of the console's kernel calls, on a virtual 256 MB address space.
When the game starts an SPU program, it runs as lifted C. Its local store is an array.
DMA becomes a memory copy through a transfer engine, and channels become message queues between threads.
